intro: If you've been searching for free llm api github repo, you've probably noticed two kinds of advice: paid tools that open with a soft upsell, and abandoned blog posts that stopped being true years ago. This one is built to stay useful, and it's maintained automatically.

We'll walk through Gemini API Free Tier, Groq Free Tier, Hugging Face Inference, and Openrouter Free Models — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Gemini API Free Tier
paragraphs: The foundation looks like this: Google's Gemini API has a free tier with per-minute and per-day model quotas — no credit card required.

In other words: You sign in with a Google account, create a key in AI Studio, and call the models over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The free tier's rate limits are more than enough for a blog that writes a few posts a day, and the paid tier is only for when you outgrow the quotas.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
bullets: Create a Google AI Studio API key
Point any OpenAI-compatible client at the Gemini OpenAI endpoint
Set LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY and LLM_MODEL and this engine writes with it

sections.heading: Groq Free Tier
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Groq offers a free tier for open-weight LLMs with some of the fastest inference speeds anywhere.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: Llama-family models run on dedicated hardware that makes response times almost embarrassing, and the free tier has enough tokens for a daily content job. It plugs into this engine through the same OpenAI-compatible interface as every other provider.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

sections.heading: Hugging Face Inference
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Hugging Face hosts thousands of open models and offers free inference access for personal projects.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? It is the natural home for open-weight models: you find the model card, read the license, and call it through the Inference Providers API. Free allowances vary by model and provider, but the catalog is the largest in the open ecosystem.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

sections.heading: Openrouter Free Models
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: OpenRouter aggregates dozens of model providers behind one API, and a set of models carry a ':free' suffix with no credit card required.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: One key, one endpoint, many backends — you can switch models in a config line and keep the same code. The free models rotate, but the pattern is stable: check the model list, pick the ones marked free, done.
Write down what you change and why — your future self will thank you.
